clue.text: Clerk given directions about copy

indicators.note: about means going round, so the compass letters surround the copy

parts.note: S and E are the compass directions south and east
a crib is a copy, as a pupil's cribbed answer

explanation.surface: An office clerk is told how to deal with a duplicate document.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe was a professional writer or copyist, a clerk keeping records.

clue.text: Biscuit soft? One's hard on edge

parts.note: a snap is a thin crisp biscuit, as in ginger snap
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
one's read as 'I is', I being one
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a biscuit has gone soft, while another is tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' stands for 'I is', the Roman numeral I for one followed by 'is', giving IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snappish is irritable and short-tempered, which is how a person on edge behaves.

clue.text: Diana leaves Crockford, for example, in church office

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the name is removed from the book's description

parts.note: Crockford's Clerical Directory is the reference book listing Church of England clergy
Di is the short form of the name Diana

explanation.surface: A woman named Diana quits her job at a clergy reference publisher.
explanation.walkthrough: Crockford's is the directory of Anglican clergy, so the surface stays churchy throughout.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the benefice or living held by a rector, an ecclesiastical post as well as the house.

clue.text: Capital punishment has a point, in essence

indicators.note: has means holds within, so the word for essence contains the point

parts.note: being is essence, the fundamental nature of something
a head is a point, as a headland or the head of a spear

explanation.surface: Someone argues that the death penalty is basically justified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is a pun: the head is the top of the body, so beheading is literally capital punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Execution by cutting off the head is a form of the death penalty, a pun on caput, head.

clue.text: Very bad time to dismiss conclusions expressed in precise terms

indicators.note: conclusions are the final letters of each word, and dismiss means they are dropped from the three words

explanation.surface: A dreadful period has to be ended, someone declares with exactness.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the last letters Y, D and E from VERY, BAD and TIME to leave VER, BA and TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means word for word, reproduced exactly as originally spoken or written.

clue.text: Toy space vehicle disintegrated, losing height — real space vehicle can make it

definitions.text: real space vehicle can make it

indicators.note: disintegrated means broken into pieces, so the toy's letters are scattered and reassembled
losing means giving up, so one letter is taken out of the toy's name

explanation.surface: A toy rocket falls apart and drops, unlike a real one that reaches orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H (height) from TOY SPACE VEHICLE and rearrange the remaining fourteen letters, as 'disintegrated' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Escape velocity is the speed a craft needs to break free of a planet's gravity, which a working rocket attains.

clue.text: What could promote obscure book?

parts.note: to blur is to obscure, making something indistinct

explanation.surface: Someone asks what might help sell a little-known volume.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'obscure' as an adjective describing the book; it is a verb meaning to blur.
explanation.definitionFit: A blurb is the short promotional text on a book jacket that advertises it.

clue.text: Goddess among a number in ancient city

indicators.note: among means placed amid, so the goddess sits within the number

parts.note: ten is a number
Hera was the Greek queen of the gods

explanation.surface: A goddess dwells with a band of followers in an old metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: Teheran, the Iranian capital, stands near the site of the old settlement of Rey and is a long-established city.

clue.text: Churchman murdered? Queen's signature brought about end of revolt

indicators.note: brought about means carried round, so the royal signature surrounds the final letter

parts.note: Mary R (Mary Regina) is how Queen Mary signed herself, R being Regina, queen

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word revolt

explanation.surface: A priest is killed after a monarch signs an order ending an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Monarchs sign with their name plus R for Rex or Regina, so a Queen Mary signs MARY R.
explanation.definitionFit: A martyr is someone killed for their faith, as a churchman slain for his beliefs would be.

clue.text: It may be featured in local Net crime. I fancy

definitions.text: It may be featured in local Net crime. I fancy

indicators.note: fancy here is an adjective meaning elaborate or fanciful, telling us the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A speaker guesses that something figures in online offences in their area.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: messages sent over the Internet would feature in online crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Messages sent over a computer network, the Net, are exactly what Internet crime may involve.

clue.text: One who's perpetually nine?

parts.note: being 'one over the eight' is British slang for being drunk, and one over eight is nine, so this is someone always drunk

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a person who never seems to age past nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is a British idiom for having drunk too much; nine is one more than eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A person addicted to drink is permanently intoxicated, always 'one over the eight'.

clue.text: Guide drug-dealer disposing of first of pot

indicators.note: disposing of means getting rid of, so a letter is dropped from the dealer

parts.note: a pusher is a person who sells illegal drugs

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the word pot

explanation.surface: A dealer offloads cannabis and acts as a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like cannabis in the dealer's stock, but only its first letter P is used.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher guides people to their seats, at a wedding or a theatre.

clue.text: Mundane one in athletic club lagging behind experts

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the numeral goes into the club's initials

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An ordinary runner in a sports club trails behind the professionals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lagging behind' is the charade signal: AIC comes after PROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means dull and ordinary, lacking poetry or imagination.

clue.text: What's turned up with boy reaching end of infancy?

definitions.text: What's turned up with boy reaching end of infancy?

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the little word up is read backwards

parts.note: Bert is a boy's name

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word infancy

explanation.surface: Someone asks what appears as a boy grows out of early childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: puberty turns up as a boy leaves childhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Puberty is the stage of growth when childhood ends and sexual maturity arrives.

clue.text: Ancient writers found in dusty libraries

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters are sitting inside the run of words dusty libraries

explanation.surface: Classical authors are discovered among musty old book collections.
explanation.definitionFit: Styli were the pointed implements used in antiquity to write on wax tablets.

clue.text: Abusive villainy in cycle of operas

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the wickedness goes into the opera cycle

parts.note: the Ring is Wagner's four-opera cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen
evil is villainy, wickedness

explanation.surface: Insulting wickedness appears in a series of operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Reviling means insulting someone harshly, so the word describes abusive speech.

clue.text: Gently treated nine during telly broadcast

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one scrambled word sits inside the other
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of telly are spread about
treated means processed or worked on, so the letters of nine are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something was handled softly as a number came up on a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' and 'broadcast' sound like television talk but are both anagram signals, and 'during' sets the jumbled nine inside the jumbled telly.
explanation.definitionFit: Leniently means mercifully or mildly, not harshly, which matches softly.

clue.text: Roman poet's supporting opening of treasure chests

indicators.note: supporting means holding up from below, so in a down answer the poet comes after the letter
opening of picks the first letter of the word treasure

parts.note: Horace was the Roman poet, and his name with 's gives the possessive

explanation.surface: A classical poet's work is held up as the key to finding treasure chests.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supporting' puts HORACE'S beneath T.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoraces is the plural of thorax, the chest cavity of the body.

clue.text: A lot of pain in face a bishop tries to control

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened pain goes into the face

parts.note: a dial is a face, as of a clock

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is cut from the pain word

parts.note: agony is great pain

explanation.surface: A churchman grimaces in pain while trying to keep order.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is the chess piece, which moves along diagonal lines.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess a bishop moves only along slanting lines, so these are the lines it tries to command.

clue.text: Try to struggle with line, with no life in acting

indicators.note: to struggle means to thrash about, so the letters of try and line are jumbled together

explanation.surface: An actor fights with a line and delivers a lifeless performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertly means sluggishly, without motion or vigour.

clue.text: Sound of horse that's close, coming round end of house

indicators.note: coming round means encircling, so the word for close surrounds the letter

parts.note: nigh means close, near

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word house

explanation.surface: A horse is heard whinnying nearby as it rounds the corner of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the high whinnying call a horse makes.

clue.text: Bookmaker's assistant whose work helps those who go to back

definitions.meaning: a person helping a book's maker by compiling its alphabetical reference list, not a betting shop clerk

definitions.text: whose work helps those who go to back
definitions.meaning: readers turn to the back of a book to find the reference list of topics and pages

explanation.surface: A betting shop clerk's job is to help punters who wager on horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookmaker' and 'back' suggest betting; here the book is a printed volume and the back is its last pages.
explanation.definitionFit: An indexer compiles the alphabetical list of topics at the end of a book.

clue.text: Exotic dancing pronounced worthless by church

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so we take the sound of the word for worthless

parts.note: naught means nothing, so worthless

explanation.surface: Someone at church condemns exotic dancing as having no value.
explanation.walkthrough: A nautch is a traditional Indian dance performed by professional dancing girls.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautch is an Indian entertainment by dancing girls, exotic to a Western reader.

clue.text: A small volume about central Serbia is bitter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the volume unit goes round the central letters

parts.note: cc (cubic centimetre) is a small unit of volume

indicators.note: central picks the middle letters of the word Serbia

explanation.surface: A short book on central Serbia makes for sour reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small volume' suggests a little book, but it is the unit cc.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerbic means sharp and sour in taste or manner, so it is a synonym for bitter.

clue.text: Disney character, one born with fairy queen turning up

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means reading upwards, so the whole run of pieces is reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Queen Mab is the fairy queen of English folklore, in Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: A Disney figure is said to be born with a fairy queen appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: In the grid the fairy queen goes upwards first, then B and I follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambi is the young deer who stars in the 1942 Disney animated film.

clue.text: Man had died in vehicle in Somerset town

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the man and the dead go into the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
he'd is the contraction of 'he had', he being a man

explanation.surface: A man died in his car in a West Country town.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a county in south-west England; Cheddar, known for its gorge and cheese, is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a place in Somerset famous for its gorge and the cheese named after it.

clue.text: Encountered part of Bible that's rejected object of worship

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: met means encountered
OT is the Old Testament, part of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone meets a section of scripture that condemns idols.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a natural object or carved figure revered as a sacred emblem of a group.

clue.text: Opposing poison shown by X (in action it varied)

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter sits within the rearranged words
varied means altered, so the letters of action it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unknown X is shown to vary when put into action, opposing poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges ACTION IT into ANTITOIC, and 'in' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antitoxic describes a substance that neutralises a toxin, counteracting poison.

clue.text: Farmland setting for country dance by Irish composer

parts.note: a hay (or hey) is an old English country dance
John Field was an Irish composer, inventor of the nocturne

explanation.surface: A rural field is the venue for a folk dance by an Irish musician.
explanation.walkthrough: John Field (1782-1837) was the Irish pianist credited with inventing the nocturne; 'by' means beside, so the composer follows the dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A hayfield is a meadow where grass is grown and cut for hay, a kind of farmland.

clue.text: Old king accepting little change in island

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the king's name holds the coin

parts.note: Cyrus the Great was an ancient Persian king
p (penny) is a small coin, little change

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch accepts a coin on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyprus is an island in the eastern Mediterranean.
